medium.title: Ahead of Market: 10 Things That Will Decide Stock Market Action on Monday
medium.summary:
Indian equities logged a fifth consecutive session of losses, weighed down by elevated crude oil prices and persistent FII outflows — both key macro headwinds with direct implications for the INR and the current account. Rising US Treasury yields are adding further pressure by making dollar-denominated assets relatively more attractive, incentivising capital outflows from emerging markets including India. Sentiment remains fragile despite intraday recoveries, suggesting limited near-term conviction among domestic participants. For INR traders, the combination of sustained FII selling and high oil — India's largest import — reinforces depreciation pressure on the rupee. Bond investors should monitor the US yield trajectory closely, as a continued rise could delay any dovish pivot expectations from the RBI and keep domestic G-Sec yields elevated. Key technical levels on Nifty (23,600 flagged as critical support) will be closely watched Monday; a breakdown could accelerate FII exits and further stress the INR.

medium.title: Gold's Next Rally Could Be Taking Shape: Why Investors Should Focus on the Bigger Picture
medium.summary:
Gold is entering a consolidation phase following a strong prior rally, with market sentiment shifting from optimism to caution — a pattern typical of bull market pauses rather than trend reversals. For INR traders and Indian market participants, gold dynamics remain macro-relevant: India is among the world's largest gold importers, and sustained or renewed gold price rallies can widen the merchandise trade deficit, exerting structural pressure on the INR/USD rate. Elevated gold prices also tend to boost domestic inflation via import costs. Investors should monitor whether gold resumes its upward trajectory, as this would have direct implications for India's current account balance, RBI FX reserve deployment, and broader INR sentiment.
